title: task create with an explicit --id that is taken reports conflict, sending callers into an unresolvable retry loop
description:
Reported by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-18 against installed 0.7.1 and REPRODUCED HERE ON DEV at 6c3af4d, so it is not one of the defects dev has already fixed.

Repro, in a scratch workspace:
  quest task create first --id TASK-89 ...      exit 0
  quest task archive TASK-89 ...                exit 0
  quest task create collision --id TASK-89 ...  exit 5

  error_type: conflict
  message:    Task state changed concurrently; the operation was not applied.
  hint:       Read the latest task state and retry the operation.

There is no concurrent writer. The id is held by an archived record at .quest/archive/tasks/TASK-89.json.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN DOCUMENTING. Our own machine contract tells a caller that on exit 5 they should re-read and perform a bounded retry. opum-cli-e2e did exactly that, three times, against a condition no retry can ever resolve. Every other signal available to them said the workspace was healthy: quest doctor reported healthy true with no issues, and task edit against the same workspace succeeded throughout. They found the cause only by listing .quest/archive on a hunch.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a deliberate mapping that is right for one case and wrong for the other. src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:450 throws task_already_exists when the id is taken in ANY retention location, which is correct. src/cli/main.ts:3476 then maps task_already_exists to conflict, and its comment states the intent plainly: an AUTO-ALLOCATED id racing a concurrent writer surfaces as task_already_exists, and there retrying recomputes a fresh id and succeeds. That reasoning is sound. It just does not hold when the caller supplied --id explicitly: the id is fixed, so the retry the hint prescribes is guaranteed to fail forever.

So one error message covers two cases with OPPOSITE remedies, and the CLI maps both to the retryable one. The discriminator is already available at the call site (src/cli/main.ts:2835 reads one(parsed, --id)); it is simply not consulted.

Shape suggested by the reporter and adopted: error_type validation, a message naming the id and that it is held by an existing record, and a hint saying to choose another id or omit --id. Naming the retention location is the part that would have saved them the hunch, since a completed or archived holder is invisible to task list.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task create with an explicit --id that is already held returns error_type validation on exit 6, not conflict on exit 5, and the message names the id.
The hint tells the caller to choose a different id or omit --id, and never tells them to retry.
The error names the retention location holding the id, so a holder invisible to task list (completed or archived) is identifiable without inspecting .quest by hand.

The auto-allocated path is unchanged: a task create WITHOUT --id that loses an id race still returns conflict with the retry hint, because there retrying does succeed. Proven by a test that exercises the auto-allocated case, not only the explicit one.
A regression test covers an explicit --id colliding with an archived record specifically, since that is the reported case and the one task list cannot show.

implementationNotes:
Fixed at the CLI call site (src/cli/main.ts, task create dispatch), not in the application layer. ProjectManager.create receives an already-resolved id and cannot tell an explicit --id from an allocated one, so only the call site holds the discriminator. The application layer is untouched: it still throws task_already_exists for a taken id in any retention location, which was always correct.

The new branch is entered only when explicitId !== undefined AND the thrown message is task_already_exists; everything else rethrows to the existing handler unchanged. The retention location is resolved with viewWithPath, which reads across every location, so the message can name .quest/archive/tasks/<id>.json -- the fact that cost the reporter a hunch to find.

AC4 IS LEFT UNCHECKED, deliberately, and here is exactly how far the evidence goes. The criterion has two clauses and they are not equally proven. The test exercises the auto-allocated case (allocation steps over an archived id and succeeds, exit 0), and the mutation run below shows that test is insensitive to this change -- it passed identically against pre-fix and post-fix code, which is evidence the auto path is unchanged. What is NOT directly observed is the clause that an auto-allocated id LOSING A RACE still returns conflict with the retry hint, because that needs two writers racing for the same allocated id and the test does not simulate concurrency. The structural argument is strong (the guard rethrows whenever explicitId is undefined, so the race cannot reach the new branch) but it is an argument, not a measurement, and a criterion checked on an argument stops anyone else from looking.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, per the fleet rule that a gate must be shown to reject as well as accept. Reverting src/cli/main.ts to HEAD and re-running the new test file gives 1 pass / 2 fail: both explicit-id tests fail with Expected 6, Received 5, and the auto-allocated test still passes. That is the predicted subset rather than a blanket red -- the mutant genuinely preserves what the third test asserts, which is what distinguishes a suite testing the property from one pinned to the implementation.

bun run check: exit 0, 592 pass / 0 fail across 72 files (589/71 before this change).
finalSummary:
task create with an explicit --id that is already held now returns validation (exit 6) naming the id and the path holding it, instead of conflict (exit 5) with a retry hint no retry could satisfy.

WHAT CHANGED. One error message covered two cases with opposite remedies. task_already_exists is thrown whenever an id is taken in any retention location, and the CLI mapped all of it to conflict. That mapping is right for an AUTO-ALLOCATED id losing a race to a concurrent writer -- retrying recomputes a fresh id and succeeds, and the existing comment says so. It is wrong for an id the caller passed with --id, which is fixed, so the prescribed retry can never succeed. The fix draws the distinction at the only place that holds it, the task create dispatch in src/cli/main.ts, and narrows nothing else: the auto-allocated path keeps conflict and its retry hint, and the application layer is unchanged.

The error also names the retention location, via viewWithPath. That is the half that matters for the reported case: the id was held by an ARCHIVED record, which task list does not show and doctor reports nothing about, so the reporter had a workspace where every reachable signal said healthy while every create failed.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. Reproduced first against dev at 6c3af4d, not only against the reporters installed 0.7.1 -- this fleet has been re-filing defects that dev had already fixed, so confirming it was still live on dev came before any code was written. Three regression tests in test/qcli346-explicit-id-taken.test.ts cover the archived holder, a live holder, and the auto-allocated path. Reverting src/cli/main.ts to HEAD turns exactly the two explicit-id tests red (Expected 6, Received 5) and leaves the auto-allocated one green -- the localised subset rather than a blanket red, which is what shows the suite tests the property rather than the implementations identity. bun run check exits 0 at 592 pass / 0 fail, up from 589.

ONE CRITERION IS LEFT UNCHECKED. AC4 asks that an auto-allocated id losing a race still returns conflict with the retry hint. The test exercises the auto-allocated case and the mutation run shows it is insensitive to this change, but the race itself is not simulated -- that needs two concurrent writers. The guard rethrows whenever no --id was supplied, so the race cannot reach the new branch, but that is an argument from the code rather than an observation, and it is recorded as such rather than ticked.

Reported by opum-cli-e2e. Ships in 0.9.0; CHANGELOG entry added under Unreleased.
